description: Canonical alumni list for thealums.com and the news bot. Merged from js/data.js, js/alumni.js, js/dictionary.js and worker/boxbot.js ROSTER on 2026-11-16. Team/espnId come from 2026 ESPN summary boxes (weeks 1-10, final games) when a player appeared in one.

notes.uid: espn:<ESPN athlete id> when the player has appeared in a 2026 ESPN box; otherwise site:<site key>. id is the site key used by js/weekN.js.
notes.site.profile: Display fields carried over from data.js/alumni.js. week1/season/fantasy inside it are the launch hand seed, NOT box-verified. Never quote them as stats; use js/weekN.js box lines.

profile.bio: The face of the modern Oregon pipeline. Herbert left Eugene as a dual-threat Heisman finalist and has become one of the NFL's most complete quarterbacks — a 6-foot-6 processor with a cannon and surprising mobility.

week1.note: Middling afternoon in a Chargers upset loss.

profile.bio: Transferred from Auburn and remade himself in Eugene. Nix led Oregon to the College Football Playoff and has settled in as Denver's starter — a high-volume passer with enough legs to stay fantasy-relevant.

week1.note: Tough road opener against Kansas City.

profile.bio: Heisman winner, program icon, and still one of the most trusted backup quarterbacks in the league. Mariota remains the elder statesman of the Oregon QB tree.
A compact, decisive runner who turned a mid-round draft slot into a featured role in Tampa. Irving is the most valuable Oregon skill player in fantasy formats right now.

week1.note: Primary back; mixed box with a receiving score.

profile.bio: Power runner out of the Oregon backfield now in a crowded San Francisco room. Depth-chart climber with weekly dart-throw appeal if injuries hit.
Deep threat who stretched the field for Nix in Eugene and is still hunting a consistent target share in Denver. Big-play profile, week-to-week volatility.

week1.note: Quiet in a stalled Broncos passing game.

profile.bio: Shifty slot and return option. Flash plays and a highlight-reel celebration style — the kind of Duck who shows up on every Sunday slate even when the box score is modest.
Transfer-portal receiver who led Oregon in receiving yards in 2025. Developmental piece in Las Vegas after a sixth-round selection.
First-round tight end who announced himself immediately — a rushing touchdown in the first five minutes of his NFL career. Big Ten TE of the Year in 2025. The rookie to watch.

week1.note: Rushing TD on his first NFL series.

profile.bio: Converted receiver who became a Saints tight end staple. Reliable red-zone target and one of the longer-tenured Ducks still producing on offense.
Athletic mismatch tight end drafted to grow in Sean McVay's offense. Year-two leap candidate.
Blocking specialist and special-teams veteran. One of the quieter, longer Oregon careers in the league.
Consensus top-three tackle in football. Left-side anchor in Detroit and the gold standard for Oregon offensive linemen. All-Pro caliber every season.

week1.note: Full-game starter. No flags of note.

profile.bio: Rimington-level interior lineman who can play guard or center. Already a Raiders building block on the interior.
Undrafted success story. Versatile interior/tackle depth who has carved out a real NFL role in Dallas.
Center/guard who stayed in the same city as Nix. Reliable depth with starting experience.
First-round tackle out of the 2025 class. Immediate starter in Washington's rebuilt line — the next Sewell-track Duck.
Third-round guard from the 2026 draft. Physical interior prospect who made Jacksonville's 53 as a rookie.
Tackle/guard swing who followed the Oregon OL factory into Dallas.
Sixth-round interior lineman joining Herbert in Los Angeles.
Still a wrecking-ball three-technique more than a decade in. The senior voice of the Duck defensive line tree.
Twelve-year veteran still starting on the interior. Sacramento-to-Eugene-to-the-league path that defined a generation of Duck linemen.
Edge rusher with first-round pedigree and a flair for the moment. Still hunting a true breakout year in New York.

week1.note: Edge snaps, pressure without a sack.

profile.bio: First-round interior defender now in Pittsburgh's always-physical front. Year-two starter with IDP upside.
Long-armed interior/edge hybrid. Rotational piece in Atlanta.
Transfer nose who joined Herbert's Chargers after one year in Eugene.
Long edge who transferred in and left as a mid-round pick. Developing pass-rush piece in Arizona.
Tackling machine from the Herbert-era defense. Special-teams ace who has grown into a regular defensive role.

week1.note: Marquee tackling day flagged in Oregon's ProDucks recap.

profile.bio: Physical linebacker now in Kansas City's always-loaded front seven.
Local product and tackling machine. Seven tackles in his NFL debut — instant impact as a rookie linebacker in Indianapolis.
Cover corner on a Super Bowl trajectory. One of the highest-paid-corner conversations in football after anchoring New England's defense.
Rangy free safety with ball skills. Now paired with Thibodeaux in New York — an all-Oregon defensive backfield look on some snaps.

week1.note: Marquee performance in Oregon's Week 1 recap.

profile.bio: Fifth-round steal who became a full-time starter in San Francisco's secondary. Physical, smart, and rarely off the field.
First-round safety after one year in Eugene (via Purdue). Earned a game ball in his NFL debut — the defensive headline of Week 1 for the Flock.

week1.note: Game ball in debut. Best Duck defensive day of Week 1.

profile.bio: Ole Miss transfer who started 13 games for Oregon in 2025. Fourth-round pick into Kansas City's secondary.
Physical safety who earned a starting job in Green Bay. Another mid-round Duck who outplayed his draft slot.

week1.note: Marquee Week 1 mention from Oregon Athletics.

profile.bio: Oregon-to-CFL quarterback. Separate board from the NFL Sunday slate.

week1.note: Tracked on the North of the Border chip.

profile.bio: Former Duck receiver in the CFL. Kept on a separate filter so the NFL board stays clean.
